text:
Harper: Heads-up: we saw a tenant hit quota-exceeded errors even though the console showed quota free. Root cause looks like provisional token allocations from retries not reflected in per-route quota accounting, so multiple branches were accepted and later confirmed -> effective quota breach and customer-visible rate-limits.
Sana: Can you paste a sanitized trace?
Harper: snippet: 
```
2026-03-27T11:02:12Z req=rq-501 route=us-east-1 tenant=alpha client_session=cs-501 toolcall_id=tc-501 provisional_hold=1 provisional_tokens=1200
2026-03-27T11:02:15Z client retried -> routed=eu-west-1 req=rq-501 client_session=cs-501 toolcall_id=(missing) provisional_hold=1 provisional_tokens=1200
2026-03-27T11:02:20Z confirm both -> ledger charged two confirms; tenant experienced quota blocks shortly after for new requests
```
Devon: So provisional allocations currently aren't subtracted from the tenant's available quota in the quota service? I thought we reserved a soft hold.
Mira: We do a soft provisional hold in the local route allocator, but per-route only. There's no global provisional hold, and the per-route quotas don't speak to each other. That allows parallel provisional accepts across routes.
Sana: That explains why the console looked "available": it reads quotas from the global quota counter which only deducts on final confirmation. The per-route local allocator was allowing provisional sessions that later confirmed.
Harper: Impact: tenant exceeded their intended concurrent-token limit briefly and subsequent requests were throttled. Also makes cost accounting messy.
Devon: We have 3 remediation axes discussed: 
- Short-term: expose "outstanding_provisional_holds" metric per-tenant and per-route in the console so ops can triage and billing can see leakage. Add a Grafana alert when outstanding_provisionals > X or when confirmed_tokens / provisional_tokens_by_tenant > 1.2 in a short window.
- Mid-term: treat provisional allocations as soft global holds in quota service: on provisional allocate, attempt to acquire a short-lived lease in central quota service (fast path cached) to decrement available quota until confirm/expiry.
- Alternative (less invasive): require flow-id propagation and gate retry acceptance at gateway: if a flow already has a provisional allocation, reject sibling retries instead of letting other routes accept them.
Sana: The gateway-flow-id gate sounds appealing because it's low-latency and avoids changing quota service, but it requires client adoption or the gateway must synthesize flow-ids deterministically. Also we'd need to decide whether synthetic flow-ids count for dedupe.
Mira: And gate-by-flow-id still fails if the retry arrives at a different gateway instance that hasn't seen the original provisional (we'd need gossip or a mini-cache). Could work best with sticky routing.
Devon: The quota-leases approach is conceptually clean but risky: adding central calls on provisional could increase p99 if not carefully cached/pooled. We could do a best-effort lease: try central quick-acquire; if fail-fast then fallback to per-route provisional but flag for reconcile.
Harper: Console UX: add a per-tenant toggle "Treat provisional as hard quota" (off by default) which when enabled forces provisional-to-acquire global lease for that tenant (useful for high-risk/enterprise tenants). Also add a new card showing "outstanding provisional holds" and "provisional -> confirmed delta" with route breakdown.
Sana: Telemetry: emit provisional_meta={route, host, flow_id?, ingress_gateway, provisional_expiry} and quota_event={type:provisional_acquire, result:local_accept|global_lease_acquired|global_lease_failed}. That will let us understand where provisional holds are escaping global accounting.
Mira: We should also add an e2e test in the routing harness that simulates truncation + retry across two routes and verifies the quota accounting path for both the gateway-gated flow-id approach and the quota-lease approach.
Devon: Ops mitigation for now: 1) add Grafana alert for confirmed_tokens_spike and outstanding_provisionals_by_tenant, 2) temporarily lower provisional TTL from 60s -> 10s for canary to reduce window where multiple accepts can happen, 3) add a reconcile job that finds tenants with provisional_vs_confirmed mismatch and creates tentative refunds or billing notes.
Harper: Agree. Also need a quick dashboard widget showing "requests_missing_flow_and_toolcall_id_pct" so we can target SDKs.
Sana: Implementation owners? Mira -> telemetry + console widget + e2e tests. Devon -> reconcile job + alert runbook + provisional TTL patch for canary. Harper -> gating design doc for global-lease vs gateway-flow-id; will convene infra and billing for trade-offs.
opsbot: created ticket BLG-2026-141 and linked to infra-queue (auto)
Devon: I'll draft the alert runbook and a short script to extract suspect traces for billing-ops.
Mira: I'll prototype the "outstanding_provisionals" metric as a tag on existing quota exporter and open PR.
Harper: Let's pick a canary timeline: provisional TTL change tonight, telemetry + dashboard early tomorrow, and design doc by EOD tomorrow. Thanks all.
Sana: ping @Mira @Devon for PR reviews when ready. :rocket:
